card.text: The Little Dumbbell Nebula is a planetary nebula about 1,359 parsecs away.

sources.label: Chornay & Walton (2021), A&A 656, A110; CDS J/A+A/656/A110, Table A.1, PN G130.9-10.5: distance 1359 pc (1190 to 1546) from the Gaia EDR3 parallax of its central star
Wikipedia, "Little Dumbbell Nebula"
sources.quote: The Little Dumbbell Nebula, also known as Messier 76, NGC 650/651, the Barbell Nebula, or the Cork Nebula, is a planetary nebula in the northern constellation of Perseus.

introduction.text: ESA/Hubble's photograph of it stands here as a flat picture facing the Sun, 1.98 pc wide.

sources.quote: It was discovered by Pierre Méchain in 1780 and included in Charles Messier's catalog of comet-like objects as number 76.

optical.summary: A flat picture facing the Sun at the nebula's distance; nothing in it has depth.
